modelReview.summary: The manuscript fails to report the core statistical result, misrepresents the exploratory nature as prespecified, and omits crucial methodological details including missingness handling and assumption diagnostics.

findings.title: Primary statistical result not reported in manuscript
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (Results section lists only sample size)
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript's abstract and conclusions are unsupported because the actual correlation coefficient, p-value, and confidence interval are not presented, making the paper uninformative.
findings.actionableFix: Incorporate the estimated correlation (0.658) and p-value (3.87e-31) with a confidence interval into the Results and Abstract. Note the sample size (240).

findings.title: Study claims prespecified question but analysis is unbound/exploratory
findings.whyItMatters: Presenting an unplanned exploratory analysis as prespecified inflates credibility and misleads readers about the confirmatory status of the finding.
findings.actionableFix: Rewrite the title, abstract, and methods to clarify that the analysis emerged from data exploration without a pre-registered protocol. Remove the word 'prespecified'.

findings.title: No description of missing data handling or excluded participants
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (mentions complete-case 240 but no exclusion details)
findings.whyItMatters: Without reporting the number of records excluded due to missing data, reasons, and a comparison of excluded vs. included characteristics, selection bias cannot be ruled out and the generalizability is unknown.
findings.actionableFix: Add a flow diagram showing eligibility and missingness. Report the number and percentage of missing values per variable, and ideally present a table comparing included and excluded subjects on key demographics if available.

findings.title: Pearson correlation assumptions not checked or reported
evidenceRefs: stats-run/correlation-scatter.png (present but not analytically assessed in manuscript)
manuscript.md (methods mention diagnostics but no details)
findings.whyItMatters: Violations of normality or linearity can yield misleading Pearson coefficients; without diagnostic reporting, the validity of the result is unsubstantiated.
findings.actionableFix: Report formal tests or visual checks for bivariate normality, linearity, and influential outliers. Consider presenting a Spearman correlation or a robust alternative alongside. Include the scatterplot with a smoothed curve.

findings.title: Descriptive statistics for variables not reported
findings.whyItMatters: The reader cannot gauge the variability or distribution shape of the correlated variables, limiting interpretation of the coefficient.
findings.actionableFix: Add a table with mean, standard deviation, median, IQR, and range for outcome_cont and severity.

findings.title: No consideration of potential confounders
findings.whyItMatters: The observed correlation could be confounded by unmeasured variables, but the analysis makes no attempt to adjust or discuss this limitation, potentially overstating the direct association.
findings.actionableFix: Either perform an adjusted partial correlation or discuss known confounders (age, sex, comorbidities) and why the unadjusted correlation remains informative. Acknowledge the lack of causal interpretation.

findings.title: No comparison with prior literature or effect size context
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (no references or discussion of expected correlation)
findings.whyItMatters: Without contextualizing the magnitude of the correlation against similar studies, the reader cannot assess whether 0.658 is plausible or clinically meaningful.
findings.actionableFix: Add a brief literature review or reference to known benchmarks for the relationship between these variables.

findings.title: Limited reproducibility information
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md (mentions artifact inventory but no analysis script)
findings.whyItMatters: Other researchers cannot easily replicate the analysis steps (e.g., data cleaning, correlation computation) without the analysis code, reducing trust and verifiability.
findings.actionableFix: Provide the analysis script (or at minimum a text description with software/version) and note whether a seed was used for any random procedures. If no random procedures, state that explicitly.
